clue.text: Being multi-talented, pop star has to drop jazz and French art

parts.note: Jacko was the tabloid nickname of the singer Michael Jackson
to drop is to fall
trad is traditional jazz
in French 'thou art' is 'tu es', so art is es

explanation.surface: A versatile performer is told to give up jazz and French art.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French art' is the verb (thou art), not painting. The definition reads as a being who is multi-talented.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone skilled at many different jobs is called this, often half-mockingly.

clue.text: Bumbling detective wants pensioner to chase gutless kids

indicators.note: to chase is to follow behind, so the pensioner piece comes after
gutless means the central letter of the word for kids is removed

parts.note: to kid is to joke, so kids gives jokes
OAP is the British abbreviation for old-age pensioner

explanation.surface: An inept sleuth needs an old man to run after cowardly children.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kids' is the verb (jokes), not children; removing the middle K leaves JOES.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for a hapless stooge, also the name of a clumsy private eye in the 1980s Eagle comic.

clue.text: Some of us may be retired but relics? That's unfair

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'Some of us may be retired but relics? That's unfair' (15): the anagram needs VICARS BUT RELICS; 'retired' cannot supply VICARS, so the printed word is likely misread beyond what printedClue allows, and no source found.
annotationWithheld.clue: Some of us may be retired but relics? That's unfair

clue.text: Steers without wheels, breaking leg

indicators.note: breaking means one piece splits the word for leg open

parts.note: on is the leg side in cricket

indicators.note: wheels means turns round, so the word for without is read backwards

parts.note: ex means without, as in ex-dividend

explanation.surface: Bullocks lose their cart wheels and one breaks a leg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Steers' suggests driving, but it is the definition; 'wheels' signals a turnaround, and the leg is the cricket leg side.
explanation.definitionFit: Steers are castrated male cattle, and oxen are cattle used as draught animals.

clue.text: Bookshop may sell this in all the best branches?

definitions.text: Bookshop may sell this in all the best branches?

parts.words: Bookshop may sell this in all the best branches?
parts.note: a Hemingway novel stocked in good bookshop branches, also read as tree branches (arms) being bid goodbye

explanation.surface: A bestseller stocked in every good bookshop chain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'branches' are shop outlets in the surface, but limbs of a tree, which are arms, in the joke.
explanation.definitionFit: Hemingway's 1929 novel of the Italian front in the First World War.

clue.text: Stories about major fraud haunt royal distiller

indicators.note: about means the word for stories goes around the other pieces

parts.note: lies are untrue stories
a big con is a large-scale swindle
a den is a favourite haunt
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for royalty

explanation.surface: Tales of a huge swindle hang about some royal whisky maker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the stories round the fraud and the haunt; ER (Elizabeth Regina) is the usual crossword royal.
explanation.definitionFit: A laboratory glassware piece that cools vapour back to liquid during distillation.

clue.text: Fixing location, traveller reveals journey

parts.note: a rep is a commercial traveller, a salesperson on the road
to air something is to reveal it
a hop is a short journey, especially a flight

explanation.surface: A salesman explains where he settled and describes his trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'traveller' is a sales representative, not a tourist.
explanation.definitionFit: A garage or workshop is where broken things are mended.

clue.text: Removal of inequality and lowering of borders flummoxed a racist

indicators.note: borders means the word for lowering lies on both sides of the other piece

parts.note: demotion is lowering in rank

indicators.note: flummoxed means confused, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Equal rights arrive and frontier controls ease, baffling a bigot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flummoxed' turns A RACIST into CRATISA, and 'borders' sets the lowering word on both sides of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Making a society more democratic spreads power and rights evenly among citizens.

clue.text: She heartlessly supports one separating identical twins?

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece goes underneath, so it comes last
separating means one piece sits inside the word for identical, splitting it

parts.note: identical means the same
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: heartlessly means the centre letter of the word she is removed

explanation.surface: A woman props up someone keeping identical twins apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supports' puts the trimmed SE below in this down clue. The question mark marks the definition as a description of twins rather than a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Conjoined twins were long called Siamese, after the famous pair from Siam.

clue.text: Always upset when miners appear in catalogue

indicators.note: appear in means the miners go inside the word for always

parts.note: e'er is a poetic contraction of ever, always
NUM is the National Union of Mineworkers
ate means troubled, as in what ate him

explanation.surface: Constantly troubled when mining men show up in a list.
explanation.walkthrough: NUM, Britain's miners' union, is a crossword staple; 'upset' gives ATE as in 'what's eating him?'.
explanation.definitionFit: To list items one by one is to name them in order.

clue.text: Flat sound comes from this through loudspeakers etc.

indicators.note: through means one piece passes inside the other

parts.note: PA is a public address system
an amp, an amplifier, is where sound comes out

explanation.surface: A dull noise comes over the speakers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flat' is the definition as a noun, a level plain, not a dull sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A pampa is a vast treeless plain of South America.

clue.text: Poet's old work briefly seen on YouTube

indicators.note: briefly means the word is shortened

parts.note: a video is a piece of work posted on YouTube

explanation.surface: A poet's early output turns up online in short form.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen on YouTube' tells you the work is a video, shortened to VID.
explanation.definitionFit: Ovid was a Roman poet, author of the Metamorphoses.

clue.text: First members of CID joined to represent third?

definitions.text: First members of CID joined to represent third?

parts.words: First members of CID joined to represent third?
parts.note: join the first two letters of CID, a curved C and a straight I, and they draw the third letter, D

explanation.surface: Senior detectives teamed up to stand in for a third party.
explanation.walkthrough: CID is the police detective branch in Britain, but here it is just three letters: C is the curved half, I the straight edge, together forming D.
explanation.definitionFit: A half circle, the shape of a letter C, joined to a straight line makes a D.

clue.text: Almost home, take from the mouth a flower

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of the word for home is lost

parts.note: the hearth is the home, the fireside

indicators.note: from the mouth means spoken, so the word for take is heard

parts.note: to take is to seize

explanation.surface: Nearly home, pick a bloom straight from the lips.
explanation.walkthrough: HEARTH loses its end; then SEASE is spoken like 'seize', as in the flower's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The wild pansy, Viola tricolor, is traditionally called heartsease.

clue.text: Relations entering pub are an issue

indicators.note: entering means the relations go inside the abbreviation for pub

parts.note: PH, public house, is the map abbreviation for a pub
references are relations, things referred to
taken as written

explanation.surface: Relatives turning up at the pub are a problem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relations' are references, not family; 'issue' is a share issue, not a problem.
explanation.definitionFit: A class of shares paying a fixed dividend before ordinary shareholders, issued by a company.

clue.text: Old Conservative? New Labour lies, innit?

indicators.note: new means made afresh, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Tory jibe that New Labour tells fibs, doesn't it?
explanation.walkthrough: 'New Labour' looks like a phrase, but 'New' is the anagram signal over LABOUR LIES INNIT.
explanation.definitionFit: The Liberal Unionists split from the Liberals over Irish Home Rule and merged with the Tories in 1912.

clue.text: Gap between seats, say, runs through frame

indicators.note: through means the other pieces run inside the word for frame

parts.note: a loom is a weaving frame
eg, for example, means say
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Space between seats, for instance, extends through the structure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' belongs to the wordplay as EG, not the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The space for one's legs in front of a seat, as on an aeroplane.

clue.text: Roman historian understood who could oppose them

parts.note: tacit means understood without being stated
us is the natural opposite of them

explanation.surface: A Roman chronicler grasped who might stand against them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'us and them' is the pairing behind the second piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacitus wrote the Annals and Histories of imperial Rome.

clue.text: On last legs suffering this complaint

indicators.note: suffering means being in a bad way, so the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: Someone on their last legs suffering from a painful condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suffering' rearranges ON LAST LEGS.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard deposits forming in the bile ducts cause a painful medical condition.

clue.text: Area covered by "love powder after bathing

indicators.note: covered by means the area letter sits inside the word for love

parts.note: TLC is tender loving care

explanation.surface: Spread over a patch, an affectionate dusting after the bath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'love' is TLC here, not O as in tennis.
explanation.definitionFit: Talcum is dusted on the skin after a bath to dry it.

clue.text: Out of order or out of order

indicators.note: out of order means jumbled, so the word for order is rearranged

parts.note: form is order, as in good form

explanation.surface: Something broken, or something wrongly arranged.
explanation.walkthrough: The repetition hides the split: 'Out of' is the definition, 'order' gives FORM, and the second 'out of order' jumbles it.
explanation.definitionFit: The preposition expresses origin or source, as in made of or derived from.

clue.text: Alternative to Italian music — answer is thus to be written in reverse

indicators.note: to be written in reverse means the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
so means thus

explanation.surface: An Italian musical alternative must be written backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: A + IS + SO read backwards gives the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: In scores the Italian word for 'or' marks an optional easier passage.

clue.text: Stay calm when cut up by caravan

indicators.note: cut up by means the word for calm is split open with the other inside

parts.note: rest is calm, repose
a train is a caravan, a line of travellers

explanation.surface: Keep your cool when a caravan cuts you off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stay calm' reads as one phrase; 'Stay' is the definition and 'calm' gives REST.
explanation.definitionFit: A stay is a check or curb, something that holds back.

clue.text: Dodgy figures assume Mister Men disguises

indicators.note: disguises means the letters are hidden in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Wrong numbers taken on by the Mister Men in disguise.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mister Men are children's book characters; 'disguises' rearranges ASSUME MISTER MEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Errors in sizing give inaccurate numbers.
